notes.text: Ye — Ye prophets and ministers.

Warfare — The time of her captivity, and misery. Double - Not twice as much as her sins deserved, but abundantly enough to answer God's design in this chastisement, which was to humble and reform them, and to warn others by their example.

The voice — An abrupt speech. Methinks I hear a voice. Wilderness - This immediately relates to the deliverance of the Jews out of Babylon, and smoothing their passage from thence to Judea, which lay through a great wilderness; but principally to their redemption by the Messiah, whose coming was ushered in by the cry of John the baptist, in the wilderness. Prepare ye the way - You to whom this work belongs. He alludes to the custom of princes who send pioneers before them to prepare the way through which they are to pass. The meaning is, God shall by his spirit so dispose mens hearts, and by his providence so order the affairs of the world, as to make way for the accomplishment of his promise. This was eminently fulfilled, when Christ, who was, and is God, blessed forever, came into the world in a visible manner.

Cry — God speaks unto his ministers. He - The prophet. All flesh - The prophet having foretold glorious things, confirms the certainty of them, by representing the vast difference between the nature, and word, and work of men and of God. All that men are or have, yea, their highest accomplishments, are but like the grass of the field, weak and vanishing, soon nipt and brought to nothing; but God's word is like himself, immutable and irresistible: and therefore as the mouth of the Lord, and not of man, hath spoken these things, so doubt not but they shall be fulfilled.

Zion — Zion or Jerusalem is the publisher, and the cities of Judah the hearers. Get up - That thy voice may be better heard. Afraid - Lest thou shouldest be found a false prophet. Say - To all my people in the several places of their abode. Behold - Take notice of this wonderful work, and glorious appearance of your God.

His arm — He shall need no succors, for his own power shall be sufficient to govern his people, and to destroy his adversaries. His reward - He comes furnished with recompences as well of blessings for his friends, as of vengeance for his enemies. His work - He carries on his work effectually: for that is said in scripture to be before a man which is in his power.

glossa.text:
*Be comforted.* As if he should say: Because your king has no compassion upon you, be comforted in Christ. It can be referred to the Gentiles, of whom the Lord says through Zechariah: *I will gather together the people of the east, and they shall be to me for a people, and I will be to them for a God ((Zach. VIII))* .

*Speak ye to the heart.* ((HIER.)) He speaks to the heart who comforts one that is sorrowful, as it is said of Sichem: *Sichem spoke to her heart, and comforted her ((Gen. XXIV))* .

*Jerusalem.* Jerusalem by the Chaldeans and by the Romans, in body and in soul; the Church tormented in body by persecutors, straitened in mind.

*Her malice.* Malice is affliction, as in that place: *If there is evil in a city which the Lord does not do ((Amos. III))*.

*It is forgiven.* The cause of consolation, the remission of sins, etc., *as far as* because they are purged and loosed by punishments.
*The voice of one crying.* ((ID.)) Mindful of this voice, the Jews sent to John to ask him: Who art thou?
*Every valley shall be exalted. He that exalts himself shall be humbled, and he that humbles himself,* etc. This the masters cry even to this day in the desert of the Churches of the Gentiles.

*And all flesh shall see.* From the first coming, caught up suddenly to the second, he says: *And all flesh shall see.*

*The mouth of the Lord.* The prophets who preached the Christ to come, namely the salvation of our God.

*What shall I cry?* ((ID.)) Not without cause does he ask: for when he had offered himself of his own accord, saying: *Behold I, send me:* he announced hard things to his own people, and now he fears the same.

*All flesh.* He who bears the image of the earthly, etc., *as far as* so man, through the successions of his ages, loses his comeliness and falls into death.
*But the word of the Lord.* The Word is Christ with his body, which is the Church.

*Sion.* ((ID.)) By Sion and Jerusalem he understands the apostles and the other teachers, whom he admonishes to preach the things they have received from the Lord, and, ascending the summits of the virtues, to teach by word and by example.

*His flock,* etc. Now by contemplation, in the time to come by vision itself: now by teaching, afterward by saving or by satisfying.

*Them that are with young.* Teachers daily bringing forth sons to God.

notes.text: Captivity — The captives.

glossa.text: *Thou hast blessed, O Lord.* ((AUG.)) A psalm on the new blessing, etc., *as far as* of the turning away of iniquity.
*Thou hast forgiven.* ((ID.)) He speaks of things to come as of things past.

notes.text: But be not ye ignorant — Whatever they are. Of this one thing - Which casts much light on the point in hand. That one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day - Moses had said, Psalm xc, 4, "A thousand years in thy sight are as one day;" which St. Peter applies with regard to the last day, so as to denote both his eternity, whereby he exceeds all measure of time in his essence and in his operation; his knowledge, to which all things past or to come are present every moment; his power, which needs no long delay, in order to bring its work to perfection; and his longsuffering, which excludes all impatience of expectation, and desire of making haste. One day is with the Lord as a thousand years - That is, in one day, in one moment he can do the work of a thousand years. Therefore he "is not slow:" he is always equally ready to fulfil his promise. And a thousand years are as one day - That is, no delay is long to God. A thousand years are as one day to the eternal God. Therefore "he is longsuffering:" he gives us space for repentance, without any inconvenience to himself. In a word, with God time passes neither slower nor swifter than is suitable to him and his economy; nor can there be any reason why it should be necessary for him either to delay or hasten the end of all things. How can we comprehend this? If we could comprehend it, St. Peter needed not to have added, with the Lord.

The Lord is not slow — As if the time fixed for it were past. Concerning his promise - Which shall surely be fulfilled in its season. But is longsuffering towards us - Children of men. Not willing that any soul, which he hath made should perish.

But the day of the Lord will come as a thief — Suddenly, unexpectedly. In which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise - Surprisingly expressed by the very sound of the original word. The elements shall melt with fervent heat - The elements seem to mean, the sun, moon, and stars; not the four, commonly so called; for air and water cannot melt, and the earth is mentioned immediately after. The earth and all the works - Whether of nature or art. That are therein shall be burned up - And has not God already abundantly provided for this?

1. By the stores of subterranean fire which are so frequently bursting out at Aetna, Vesuvius, Hecla, and many other burning mountains.

2. By the ethereal (vulgarly called electrical) fire, diffused through the whole globe; which, if the secret chain that now binds it up were loosed, would immediately dissolve the whole frame of nature.

3. By comets, one of which, if it touch the earth in its course toward the sun, must needs strike it into that abyss of fire; if in its return from the sun, when it is heated, as a great man computes, two thousand times hotter than a red-hot cannonball, it must destroy all vegetables and animals long before their contact, and soon after burn it up.

Seeing then that all these things are dissolved — To the eye of faith it appears as done already. All these things - Mentioned before; all that are included in that scriptural expression, "the heavens and the earth;" that is, the universe. On the fourth day God made the stars, Gen. i, 16, which will be dissolved together with the earth. They are deceived, therefore, who restrain either the history of the creation, or this description of the destruction, of the world to the earth and lower heavens; imagining the stars to be more ancient than the earth, and to survive it. Both the dissolution and renovation are ascribed, not to the one heaven which surrounds the earth, but to the heavens in general, ver. 10, 13, without any restriction or limitation. What persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation - With men. And godliness - Toward your Creator.
Hastening on — As it were by your earnest desires and fervent prayers. The coming of the day of God - Many myriads of days he grants to men: one, the last, is the day of God himself.

We look for new heavens and a new earth — Raised as it were out of the ashes of the old; we look for an entire new state of things. Wherein dwelleth righteousness - Only righteous spirits. How great a mystery!

labour that whenever he cometh ye may be found in peace — May meet him without terror, being sprinkled with his blood, and sanctified by his Spirit, so as to be without spot and blameless. Isaiah lxv, 17; Isaiah lxvi, 22.

And account the longsuffering of the Lord salvation — Not only designed to lead men to repentance, but actually conducing thereto: a precious means of saving many more souls. As our beloved brother Paul also hath written to you - This refers not only to the single sentence preceding, but to all that went before. St. Paul had written to the same effect concerning the end of the world, in several parts of his epistles, and particularly in his Epistle to the Hebrews. Rom. ii, 4.

glossa.text:
*But this one thing.* It being proved that the judgment shall truly be, he shows how effectual it shall be. If it be said to you by the false ones: You can do what you will, because so great a time remains until the day of judgment, that from the length of time the judge will not be able to know many things; believe them not, because whatsoever can be done in a thousand years, he sees it even as that which is done in one day. If they say: In a thousand years, by repenting, you shall not obtain pardon of your offences; believe them not: because one day of true penitence avails as much unto salvation as a thousand years, as it did for the thief.

*As a thousand years. ((BEDA.))* In the acknowledgment of the divine power, etc., *as far as* whence also it is rightly subjoined:

*The Lord delayeth not.* And because he sees all things, you may believe that the Lord delays not in fulfilling his promises, because the time is not yet in which he shall fulfil the things to be fulfilled. But he therefore defers, that he may first fill up the sum of the elect which he foresaw; whence in the Apocalypse: *And it was said to them that they should rest yet a little time, until their fellow servants be filled up ((Apoc. VI))*.

*The heavens with a great violence. The heavens,* that is, the saints; if therefore there be anything in them to be purged, it shall be purged by fire.

*The elements. ((BEDA.))*, of which the world consists, etc., *as far as* and through a temporal punishment, they shall be dissolved into something better.

*But new heavens. ((ID.))* He saith not, *others,* but that the old and ancient ones are to be changed into something better, etc., *as far as* we have it also in the prophets: *The light of the lamp shall shine there no more ((Isa. LXV))*.

*Be diligent to be unspotted and undefiled.* These are the watchings of which it is said: *Blessed are those servants whom the Lord, when he cometh, shall find watching.* He watches who keeps himself free from defilements, who, as much as in him lies, has peace with all men, who subjects all the allurements of the flesh to the governance of the spirit, enjoying in himself a most happy peace.
*Our brother. ((BEDA.))* He says that Paul had written to them, wherein he shows, etc., *as far as* and by these may stir themselves up unto advancement.

Preaching the baptism of repentance — That is, preaching repentance, and baptizing as a sign and means of it.

glossa.text:
*The beginning of the Gospel. ((ISID.))* The Gospel, *good tidings,* which belongs properly to the kingdom of God and to the remission of sins. Whence: *Repent ye and believe the Gospel: and the kingdom of heaven hath drawn nigh.* 

((HIER.)) The four Gospels are one, and the one is four. And so the book of Mark also is called the Gospel, and likewise that of the others: because all are one, and one is all.

*Of Jesus Christ. ((HIER.))* Jesus in Hebrew, Soter in Greek, Salvator in Latin, Christus in Greek, Messias in Hebrew, anointed in Latin, that is, king and priest: he is said to be of the line of David the king, and of the Levitical line.

*Of the Son of God. ((BEDA.))* Matthew says: *of the son of David, the son of Abraham ((Matth. I))*. Mark says: *of the Son of God,* so that little by little from the lesser to the greater, etc., *as far as* John begins from the eternity of the Word of God, and ends in the resurrection of the Lord.

*As it is written.* Mark sets the testimonies of the prophets first, by which he asserts that these things are old and not new, but foreknown and foretold by the prophets, and in this he invites also the Jews, who had received the law and the prophets, to the Gospel: and he calls the Gentiles, who held the Gospel, to the veneration of the law and the prophets, that no one, after the heretics, may receive the one without the other.

*Behold, I send. ((BEDA.))* John is called an angel not by fellowship of nature, as Origen falsely pretends, but by the dignity of his office: as the priests also are, of whom it is said: *The lips of the priest keep knowledge, and they seek the law out of his mouth, because he is the angel of the Lord of hosts ((Mal. II))*.

((ID.)) Note that this testimony: *Behold, I send my angel,* etc., is Malachi's, yet he says that both are Isaiah's, because, etc., *as far as* all the prophets spoke by one spirit as with one mouth.

*Of one crying. ((ISID.))* To the Jews, deaf because of their sins, set far off, worthy of a cry of indignation. *In the desert.* In the desert the voice and the cry are made: because the house of Judaea is deserted, standing empty and swept, without the Spirit of God, without prophet, king, priest. Whence Jesus and John seek what was lost in the desert. Where the devil conquered, there he is conquered: where man fell, there he rises again.

*Prepare ye. ((ISID.))* Do penance and preach. Whence the Parasceve before the sabbath, etc., *as far as* that we, being at rest, may possess the desirable land.

*The way of the Lord. ((HIER.))* The way of the Lord by which he enters in unto men is penance, through which God comes down to us, and we ascend to him. Whence the angels are remembered as ascending and descending upon the Son of man.

*Make straight the paths. ((ISID.))* He commands that, going by the royal road, we love our neighbours as ourselves, and ourselves, etc., *as far as* that the mouth be not sundered from the work, nor the work from the mouth.

The paths come after the way, because the moral commandments are expounded after penance, according to Mark or Matthew. The way is prepared by faith and baptism and penance.

The paths are made straight by the austere tokens of raiment, of girdle, of food, of drink, of a most humble voice.

*John. ((ISID.))* The grace of God. He begins from the grace of God, whence there follows: *Baptizing,* etc. Through baptism sins are forgiven; whence: That which *ye have freely received, freely give ((Matth. X))*. And the Apostle: *By grace ye are saved ((Ephes. II))*.

*Baptizing. ((HIER.))* He gave the baptism of penance, he preached a baptism unto the remission of sins, yet he did not give it. As by preaching, etc., *as far as* now the bride is brought in by the friend of the bridegroom, as Rebecca to Isaac, veiled by the servant with a white cloak.

*In the Jordan ((ID.))* Jordan is the descent of another, where sins are loosed. For the ark, etc., *as far as* the body of Christ profits not those who are not cleansed, but changes them for the worse.

*Confessing,* etc. *((ID.)) Confession and beauty are in his sight ((Psal. CXV))*, that is, in the sight of the bridegroom. Whence the bride alights from her camel, when the Church humbles herself to Christ, who is figured by Isaac, at whose birth God made laughter for Sara. As it is said to Mary, who is a princess with God: *Blessed art thou among women ((Luc. I))*.

 ((BEDA.)) Confessing their sins, they are baptized. For they ought to promise the newness of a better life, who baptism, etc., *as far as* and so change those who are cleansed and promise the Christian religion into members of the Church.

*And John was,* etc. ((HIER.)) The prophet's raiment and food and drink signify the whole austere life of preachers, and the Gentiles, etc., *as far as* because all things are from the grace of the Gospel, in which there is no distinction of Jew and Greek.

*((BEDA.)) Clothed with camel's hair.* Because he did not cherish sins, but rebuked them sharply, saying: *Ye brood of vipers,* etc. The leathern girdle, etc., *as far as* for in the honey is sweetness, in the locust a nimble flight, but one soon falling.

*Mightier than I. ((HIER.))* Who is mightier than the grace by which sins are washed away? He who, etc., *as far as* and it reaches even to the hundred and forty-four thousand.

*To loose the latchet. ((BEDA.))* There was a custom among the ancients, that if any man were unwilling to take to wife her who fell to him, he, etc., *as far as* I am not able to bare the feet of the Redeemer, because I claim not for myself the name of bridegroom.

((HIER.)) The latchet of the shoes, that is, the mystery of the Incarnation of God. For the heel, etc., *as far as* the bride among the patriarchs, the friend among the prophets, the neighbour in Mary and Joseph, the beloved in John the Baptist, the dove in Christ and the apostles.

*I have baptized you with water. ((BEDA.))* John does not yet say openly that he is God or the Son of God, because his hearers were untaught: but little by little, through the humanity glorified, he leads them to faith in the divinity, saying: *But he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost.* Yet afterwards, when he saw them now more capable, he preaches the Son of God openly, saying: *He gave testimony, that this is the Son of God ((Joan. III))*.

*((ISID.)) I baptize you with water, he,* etc. The river of God is always full, always equal, of which: *The stream of the river maketh the city of God joyful ((Psal. XLV))*. There is a great distance, etc., *as far as* the anointing of Christ comes from the bitterness of the passion to the glory of the resurrection; whence the Apostle: *Have this mind in you, which was also in Christ Jesus,* etc., even to: *For which cause God also hath exalted him ((Phil. II))*.

echoes.text: For a thousand years in your sight are just like yesterday when it is past, like a watch in the night.
echoes.note: 'One day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day' restates the psalm's 'a thousand years in your sight are but as yesterday when it is past' — God's time is not man's, answering the charge of delay.

echoes.text: Have I any pleasure in the death of the wicked? says the Lord Yahweh; and not rather that he should return from his way, and live?
echoes.note: 'Not wishing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance' reflects the LORD's declaration, 'Have I any pleasure in the death of the wicked… and not rather that he should turn from his way and live?'

echoes.text: All of the army of the sky will be dissolved. The sky will be rolled up like a scroll, and all its armies will fade away, as a leaf fades from off a vine or a fig tree.
echoes.note: 'The heavens will pass away… the host of heaven shall rot away, and the skies roll up like a scroll' is the prophetic dissolution of the heavens behind 'the heavens will pass away with a great noise, and the elements will be dissolved.'

echoes.text: For the vision is yet for the appointed time, and it hurries toward the end, and won’t prove false. Though it takes time, wait for it; because it will surely come. It won’t delay.
echoes.note: 'The Lord is not slow concerning his promise' answers the vision that 'awaits its appointed time… if it seems slow, wait for it; it will surely come.'
echoes.lxxText: For the vision is yet for a time, and it shall shoot forth at the end, and not in vain: though he should tarry, wait for him; for he will surely come, and will not tarry.

echoes.text: Tear your heart, and not your garments, and turn to Yahweh, your God; for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and relents from sending calamity.
echoes.note: God 'gracious and merciful, slow to anger… and relents over disaster' grounds the patience that defers judgment for repentance (cf. Jonah 4:2).

echoes.text: The mountains melt under him, and the valleys split apart, like wax before the fire, like waters that are poured down a steep place.
echoes.note: 'The mountains will melt… like wax before the fire' supplies the melting-by-fire imagery of the day of the Lord.

echoes.text: “For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth; and the former things shall not be remembered, nor come into mind.
echoes.note: 'New heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells' draws directly on 'I create new heavens and a new earth,' the prophetic promise of a renewed creation.

echoes.text: “For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me,” says Yahweh, “so your seed and your name shall remain.
echoes.note: 'The new heavens and the new earth that I make shall remain before me' is the companion promise behind Peter's hope of the abiding new creation where righteousness is at home.

echoes.text: Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look on the earth beneath; for the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment; and those who dwell therein shall die in the same way: but my salvation shall be forever, and my righteousness shall not be abolished.
echoes.note: 'The heavens vanish like smoke, the earth will wear out like a garment… but my salvation will be forever' frames the dissolution-and-enduring-righteousness contrast Peter draws.

echoes.text: Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to deliver them in the day of Yahweh’s wrath, but the whole land will be devoured by the fire of his jealousy; for he will make an end, yes, a terrible end, of all those who dwell in the land.
echoes.note: 'In the fire of his jealousy all the earth shall be consumed' is a further day-of-the-LORD-by-fire antecedent for the burning heavens and melting elements.

echoes.text: Whoever offers a sacrifice of peace offerings to Yahweh to accomplish a vow, or for a freewill offering, of the herd or of the flock, it shall be perfect to be accepted. It shall have no defect.
echoes.note: Being found 'without defect and blameless' uses the cultic language of the unblemished offering applied to the readers' moral state at the coming.

echoes.text: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news, who publishes peace, who brings good news of good, who publishes salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns!”
echoes.note: Mark's programmatic noun 'gospel/good news' (euangelion) leans on Isaiah's herald who publishes 'good news' that 'your God reigns.' Volume is conceptual rather than verbal in 1:1 itself, but recurrence is strong: Mark returns to Isaianic euangelizō language at 1:14-15 (the reign of God). Coherence is high since the whole Gospel frames itself as the announcement Isaiah anticipated.

echoes.text: You who tell good news to Zion, go up on a high mountain. You who tell good news to Jerusalem, lift up your voice with strength. Lift it up. Don’t be afraid. Say to the cities of Judah, “Behold, your God!”
echoes.note: Isaiah 40:9 pairs 'good tidings' with Zion's herald immediately before the 40:3 'voice in the wilderness' that Mark quotes in 1:3. The proximity of the two Isaiah loci makes it likely Mark heard 'gospel' from this same context. Volume is low in v.1 but the deliberate quotation of 40:3 two verses later raises availability and coherence.

echoes.text: I will tell of the decree. Yahweh said to me, “You are my son. Today I have become your father.
echoes.note: The title 'Son of God' in the superscription anticipates the divine voice of 1:11, which quotes Psalm 2:7. Volume in v.1 is a single title, but recurrence within the chapter (and at 9:7; 15:39) gives the royal-sonship reading strong coherence. The superscription programmatically front-loads the enthronement language Mark unpacks at the baptism.

echoes.text: The Spirit of the Lord Yahweh is on me; because Yahweh has anointed me to preach good news to the humble. He has sent me to bind up the broken hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to those who are bound;
echoes.note: The Servant 'anointed to bring good news' supplies another Isaianic root for Mark's euangelion. Verbal contact is faint here and the link is largely thematic; included for maximal coverage because Mark's Jesus is the Spirit-anointed herald (cf. 1:10).
echoes.lxxText: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me; he has sent me to preach glad tidings to the poor, to heal the broken in heart, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and recovery of sight to the blind;

echoes.text: I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men;
echoes.note: Nathan's dynastic oracle ('I will be his father, he shall be my son') stands behind the messianic 'Son of God' title alongside Psalm 2. Verbal volume in Mark is minimal; the link is by way of the Davidic sonship tradition rather than direct citation, hence low and contested.

echoes.text: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
echoes.note: 'The beginning' (archē) may evoke the Genesis incipit, casting Jesus' advent as a new creation. Volume is one word and many read 'beginning' merely as a heading for the narrative, so the echo is genuinely contested; coherence rises only if Mark intends a creation-typology, which 1:10-13 (Spirit, wilderness, wild beasts) may support.

echoes.text: “Behold, I send my messenger, and he will prepare the way before me; and the Lord, whom you seek, will suddenly come to his temple; and the messenger of the covenant, whom you desire, behold, he comes!” says Yahweh of Armies.
echoes.note: Mark's 'Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way' is a near-verbatim citation of Malachi 3:1, though Mark misattributes the fused text to 'Isaiah.' Volume is maximal (sustained verbal repetition), and recurrence is confirmed by Mark 9:11-13, where the Elijah-messenger of Malachi is again applied to John. Coherence is total: the messenger prepares the way of the Lord.

echoes.text: “Behold, I send an angel before you, to keep you by the way, and to bring you into the place which I have prepared.
echoes.note: The opening clause 'Behold, I send my messenger before your face' matches Exodus 23:20 LXX (the angel guarding Israel on the wilderness road) even more closely than Malachi for the first half. Mark has conflated Exodus 23:20 with Malachi 3:1; the shared 'before your face' wording and new-Exodus 'way' imagery give high volume and coherence to a deliberate fusion.

echoes.text: The voice of one who calls out, “Prepare the way of Yahweh in the wilderness! Make a level highway in the desert for our God.
echoes.note: 'The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make ready the way of the Lord' quotes Isaiah 40:3 (LXX), the only part Mark's 'as written in Isaiah' formula actually names. Volume is maximal and the wilderness/way motif structures the whole prologue (John baptizes 'in the wilderness,' 1:4). The new-Exodus comfort-of-Zion context is highly coherent with Mark's gospel announcement.

echoes.text: They answered him, “He was a hairy man, and wearing a leather belt around his waist.” He said, “It is Elijah the Tishbite.”
echoes.note: John's garb of camel's hair and a leather belt around the waist deliberately mirrors Elijah, 'a hairy man with a leather belt around his waist' (2 Kings 1:8 LXX, zōnēn dermatinēn perthan identical phrase). High volume in a distinctive sartorial detail; recurrence at Mark 9:13 ('Elijah has come') confirms the identification. Coherence is strong: John is the returning Elijah of Malachi.

echoes.text: Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the great and terrible day of Yahweh comes.
echoes.note: Malachi 4:5 (3:23 MT) promises Elijah's return 'before the great day of the LORD'; Mark casts John in this role, fusing it with the messenger of Malachi 3:1. Verbal volume in 1:2-8 is indirect, but the Elijah dress (v.6) and Mark 9:11-13 make the figural identification explicit and recurrent. Coherence is the engine of the whole prologue.

echoes.text: It will happen in that day, that the prophets will each be ashamed of his vision, when he prophesies; neither will they wear a hairy mantle to deceive:
echoes.note: Zechariah 13:4 mentions prophets wearing 'a hairy mantle' as a deceptive sign; some see John's camel-hair garment drawing on the generic prophetic-mantle convention rather than Elijah specifically. Volume is low and the negative valence in Zechariah weakens coherence; included as a contested alternate source for the prophet's dress.

echoes.text: Even of these you may eat: any kind of locust, any kind of katydid, any kind of cricket, and any kind of grasshopper.
echoes.note: John's diet of locusts reflects the one insect category Leviticus 11:22 permits as clean food, anchoring his wilderness asceticism in Torah dietary law. The contact is a single permitted-food detail with no verbal borrowing, so the echo is faint and contested; it functions mainly to authenticate his wilderness piety.

registers.label: Spare
lines: A voice cries out in the wilderness.
Prepare the way of the Lord.
Make the rough places a level road.
Every valley shall be lifted up.
One is coming whose sandal we cannot untie.
We wait for him in the wilderness.
Come, let us worship and ready the way.
Come, Lord Jesus. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Out in the wilderness a voice is crying — clear the road, fill the valleys, bring down the hills, and make a straight way home.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
Comfort, comfort my people, says your God; the warfare is ended, the long exile done.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
He will feed his flock like a shepherd, gather the lambs close, and carry the weary in his arms.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
So we step into the wilderness to wait, and we make the road ready for our God.
Come, Lord Jesus, come. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: A voice cries out across the wilderness.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
Make the road straight; fill every valley.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
The Shepherd gathers the lambs in his arms.
Come, Lord Jesus, come.
Come, let us worship and prepare the way.
Come, Lord Jesus, come. Amen.
